look_here_first: Start with an open, wispy annual, heads at several heights, and yellow RAY + DISC florets. For the dangerous Amphiachyris amoena lookalike, inspect SIDE/BACK of phyllaries for possible green nerve borders and especially the tiny DISC-pappus scales. Habit and flower color alone cannot confirm.

key_traits.label: Life cycle
key_traits.text: Annual, herbaceous single taprooted base; not a woody perennial.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: 10–80(–100) cm, open paniculiform heads at varying heights and wiry photosynthetic branches.

key_traits.label: Stems
key_traits.text: Green resinous slender glabrous, often angled; lower leaves reduced by flowering.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Alternate very narrow, simple, often sessile, resin-gland dotted, reduced distally.

key_traits.label: Flowers
key_traits.text: Small radiate yellow heads, ray florets around disc florets. FNA species 5–23 rays and 7–48 discs; local variety often about 6–8 rays and 8–13 discs.

key_traits.label: Phyllaries
key_traits.text: Small overlapping bracts under head; a narrow green nerve border may be visible, but this is VARIABLE and not definitive.

key_traits.label: Pappus
key_traits.text: Very short scales or effectively absent in local var. texana; Amphiachyris typically has longer conspicuous disc-floret scales. Macro needed.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Minute hairy cypsela; retain adult ray-vs-disc assignment before comparing pappus.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: Open, wispy annual rather than woody-based subshrub; Heads at different branching levels; Yellow rays and discs; small green resinous branches; Possible green phyllary nerve borders; Extremely short disc pappus

lookalikes.differences: A. amoena can also show open arrays. G. texana var. texana has very short/absent disc pappus scales and sometimes a green nerve border on phyllaries; Amphiachyris disc pappus is conspicuous and phyllaries lack the green nerve border. A. dracunculoides is usually more corymbiform. Perennial snakeweed species have woody bases.
